entry.title: 1 November 2026
entry.content:
• Corrected: how the queue works no longer says the anti-bot checks look for VPNs, which no source says. It now gives the official 2025 advice instead: one tab or device per IP address, and no refreshing once you're in the queue.
  • Updated: the scams guide now points people who can't go to the official refund, with its £25 charge and deadline.
  • Updated: the FAQ answer on buying from outside the UK now gives the 2027 card rule (Visa or Mastercard credit cards only) and links to buying Glastonbury tickets from abroad.
  • Updated: more links between guides, so the glossary of ticket terms, the scams guide and your first go at Glastonbury tickets are easier to reach.

entry.title: 31 October 2026
entry.content:
• New: buying Glastonbury tickets from abroad: registering from outside the UK, the credit card rule for international buyers, a UK friend booking for you, paying the balance, and how tickets reach the EU and the rest of the world.
  • Updated: taking children and teenagers to Glastonbury now starts with how old you have to be: a table of the rules at 12 and under, 13 to 15, 16 and 17, what a responsible adult is, the TEEN ticket, the exit and re-entry wristband for 13 to 15 year olds, and the 2027 rules for children's coach seats.
  • Corrected: saving for the £308 balance over about six months comes to roughly £51 a month, not £52, in the balance payment guide, deposits and balance payments and what Glastonbury 2027 costs.
  • Updated: shorter summaries for fifteen guides, so they aren't cut off in search results.

entry.title: 30 October 2026
entry.content:
• Updated: Glastonbury 2027 balance payment and what to do before June now says when 2027 tickets will be posted (late May to June, signed for), where they go, and how coach passengers get theirs.
  • Updated: Glastonbury ticket tips, the ticket day checklist, phone or laptop: setting up either and lost your registration number? now rest on the festival's information page and live news reports, after the 2027 sale FAQ and the old ticket information page stopped working. The advice on tabs and devices now gives the festival's own reason: you'll lose your place in the queue.
  • Updated: how fast Glastonbury tickets sell out now takes its 2025 sell-out times from NME, after an older report was taken down. The times are unchanged.

entry.title: 29 October 2026
entry.content:
• New: Glastonbury 2027 local resident tickets: the inner and outer zone towns, the full weekend sale times on Sunday 1 November 2026, the deposit and balance, proof of address and what to have ready.
  • Updated: how the queue works, the checkout guide and the 2027 resale now rest on the festival's information page and live news reports, after two of their old sources stopped working.
  • New: Glastonbury 2027 Sunday tickets: who can buy them (Mendip and Central Somerset residents only), the sale at 11am on Sunday 1 November 2026, the price with the bus, children's bus tickets, refunds and what to have ready.
  • Updated: the next Glastonbury ticket sale and 2027 key dates now include the local full weekend and Sunday ticket sale on Sunday 1 November 2026, which comes before the spring resale for people who live in the qualifying areas. Other ways to get to Glastonbury now gives the 2027 Sunday ticket details, and the dates calendar has the sale.
  • Updated: how to register now says registration is suspended around the local sale and will reopen later in the autumn, as the festival now says.
  • Updated: deposits and balance payments now gives the 2027 rule for an unpaid balance: the deposit is refunded less the administration charge.

entry.title: 28 October 2026
entry.content:
• New: Glastonbury 2027 car parking: what a car park pass costs, buying one with your balance, who can't use a general pass, sharing a car, and the festival's advice on arriving and leaving by car.
  • Corrected: the campervans guide no longer says how many people or cars one car park pass covers, because the festival doesn't say. It now explains that Worthy View needs its own parking pass. The access requirements guide now says accessible parking is applied for through the Access Application.
  • New: Glastonbury ticket refunds: the 2027 refund deadline, the administration charge, what Refund Protection covers and what to do when someone in your group drops out.
  • Updated: the access requirements guide now gives the final deadline for Access Applications listed by the festival, and how to ask for the form. The deposits guide now links to the refund rules.
  • Rechecked against the festival's pages on 28 October 2026: the ticket price, deposit, balance, balance window and festival dates are unchanged.

entry.title: 26 October 2026
entry.content:
• Guides now have a named author, Jonathan Connolly. See About.
  • New: when is the next Glastonbury ticket sale?, one page we keep up to date for every sale, starting with the 2027 resale and the 2028 sale.
  • Clearer: the 2027 campervan, tipi and car park prices now say they're as listed on the festival's information page on 26 October 2026, with a link, so you can check them before you book. Buying from outside the UK now has its own part of the checkout guide and an FAQ answer.
  • Reorganised after a review of the whole site, so each guide answers one question and each fact has one home:
  • Merged: paying and booking problems are now one checkout guide; the ticket day mistakes are part of the checklist; the two tool guides are now one guide. Old links redirect to the new pages.
  • Renamed and moved: the resale guide is now Glastonbury 2027 resale, with what's known so far for 2027. Buying for a group is now the Glastonbury syndicate guide. What to do after booking now leads with the 2027 balance payment.
  • New: a free spreadsheet template, volunteering at Glastonbury 2027 and what Glastonbury 2027 costs.
  • Expanded: registration now has step by step instructions, when registration reopens and how to change your details; the queue guide explains the queue's screens and errors.
  • Easier to use: calendar files for the balance window and the festival, a chart of sell-out times, a tickable and printable checklist, a copy button on every ready-made message, and screenshots of the tool.
  • Also new: finding or changing your registration, campervans, camping and parking, how common ticket scams are in the scams guide, and a short video in the tool guide.
  • Hear about new dates without signing up: subscribe to the 2027 dates calendar and new dates, like the resale, appear in your calendar app. Or follow this page in a feed reader with its feed.
  • In the tool: groups of five or six now show a note that resale bookings have been limited to four people, and a message like "here's mine! Sam..." now picks out Sam.
  • Six new guides with tips for the current ticket system: how to get Glastonbury tickets, your first go at Glastonbury tickets, setting up your phone or laptop, what to do if checkout fails, collecting registration numbers from WhatsApp and using Glasto Quick Copy at the front of the queue.
  • Updated: the ticket day checklist and how the queue works now follow the official 2027 sale FAQ: be in the waiting room at least 10 minutes before the sale, not just a few minutes.
  • A new FAQ answer on whether there's a trick to getting tickets.
  • Corrections after a full fact check of every guide: 2024 tickets cost £360 including the booking fee, with a £75 deposit (we had £355), so the 2024 to 2025 price rise was about 5%, not 7%. The 10 minutes at the front of recent sales was for the page where you enter registration details; payment has had its own, shorter timer. The rule that registrations could be locked for 10 minutes comes from the 2025 resale. Random places in the queue still apply when a sale opens, not just in earlier sales. The guides now say the payee name "The Way Ahead Group" can appear when paying with Apple Pay or Google Pay. The savings tip is now the same in every guide (about £52 a month), and the cancellation cut-off no longer gives a date we couldn't confirm.
  • Every guide rechecked against its sources on 26 October 2026.

entry.title: 20 October 2026
entry.content:
• Ten new guides: 2027 key dates, recent sales compared, what to do after booking, paying for tickets, coach tickets, access requirements, children and teenagers, other ways to get to Glastonbury, ticket scams and a glossary.
  • Ready-to-send messages for your group chat, from collecting details to paying each other back: messages to send your group.
  • Updated for the 2027 sale results: sell-out times, the new queue, the April 2027 balance window and postage costs.
  • Corrections: the resale allowed up to four general admission tickets per booking in 2025, not two (two was the limit for coach packages). Refund and cancellation terms now say which year they come from.
  • Every existing guide expanded with worked examples, group plans and troubleshooting.
  • Guides grouped by topic on the guides page.
  • The tool's working screens no longer show ads. Ads appear only on the home page and the guides and information pages.

entry.title: 6 October 2026
entry.content:
• Guides, FAQ and information pages published alongside the tool.
  • The tool learned to read WhatsApp chats where details are on separate lines.
  • Share links number repeated first names instead of including surnames.
  • Groups and links are cleared on a seasonal schedule.
  • A visit counter on the home page.

entry.title: 5 October 2026
entry.content:
• A redesigned tool with a practice demo.
  • A public check that the live site matches the published code, every six hours.
